subject: Civic Education
examFormat: Two papers taken as a composite paper at one sitting. Paper 1: a 1-hour multiple-choice test of fifty questions drawn from the entire syllabus, carrying 40 marks. Paper 2: a 2-hour essay test in three sections (A: national ethics, discipline, rights and obligations; B: emerging issues in the society; C: governmental system and processes), each with three questions; candidates answer four questions, choosing at least one from each section, for 60 marks.

topics.name: Values
objectives: Define values
Identify the types of values
Explain the importance of values to the society

topics.name: Citizenship and Nationalism
objectives: Explain the meaning of citizenship
Explain the meaning of citizenship education
State the goals of citizenship education
Identify the duties and obligations of citizens
Explain the meaning of nationalism
Identify ways of promoting national consciousness, integrity and unity in the society
Describe the nationalistic roles of individuals and groups
Identify local and world civic problems

topics.name: Human Rights
objectives: Explain the meaning of human rights
Identify the categories of human rights
State the characteristics of human rights
Explain the meaning and historical background of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR)
Explain and identify the seven core freedoms of the UDHR
State the importance of the UDHR
Describe the roles of individuals, groups and government in the UDHR
Identify the limitations to the exercise of human rights

topics.name: Law and Order
objectives: Define law and order
State the features of law and order
Explain the importance of law and order in the society
Explain the meaning of constituted authority
Identify the types of constituted authority
Explain the importance and roles of constituted authority

topics.name: Responsible Parenthood
objectives: Explain the meaning of responsible parenthood
Describe the roles of responsible parents
Explain the importance of responsible parenthood in national development

topics.name: Traffic Regulations
objectives: Explain the meaning of traffic regulations
Explain traffic regulation and its importance in the society
Describe the roles of the individual and government in maintaining traffic regulations

topics.name: Inter-Personal Relationships
objectives: Explain the meaning of inter-personal relationships
Identify the types of interpersonal relationships
Identify skills that promote interpersonal relationships
Explain the meaning of inter-communal relationships
State the importance of inter-communal relationships
Explain the meaning of inter-communal conflicts
Identify skills for resolving inter-communal conflicts

topics.name: Cultism
objectives: Explain the meaning and origin of cultism
Identify different cult groups in Nigeria and their symbols
State the reasons for cultism
State the consequences of cultism
Identify ways of preventing cultism in the society

topics.name: Drugs and Drug Abuse
objectives: Explain the meaning of drug abuse
Identify drugs that can be abused
Describe how drugs are abused
Identify the symptoms of drug abuse
Describe the behaviours of drug addicts
Identify ways of preventing drug abuse
Identify government agencies working to prevent drug abuse/trafficking and their activities
Identify laws against drug abuse

topics.name: Human Trafficking
objectives: Explain the meaning of human trafficking
State the causes of human trafficking
State the effects and consequences of human trafficking
Describe the efforts of government and individuals in stopping human trafficking

topics.name: HIV/AIDS
objectives: Explain the meaning of HIV/AIDS
State the causes of HIV/AIDS
Identify the symptoms and effects of HIV/AIDS
Identify ways of preventing HIV/AIDS
Explain the stigmatization of people living with HIV/AIDS

topics.name: Youth Empowerment
objectives: Explain the meaning of youth empowerment
Identify youth empowerment skills
State the importance and benefits of youth empowerment skills
Describe the efforts of government towards youth empowerment

topics.name: Structure and Functions of Government
objectives: Explain the meaning of government
Identify the structure/tiers of government
State the functions of government

topics.name: Democracy, Rule of Law and National Development
objectives: Explain the meaning, types and features of democracy
State the importance of democracy
Identify the pillars of democracy
Identify the problems of democracy
Explain the meaning of rule of law
State the features of the rule of law
State the importance of the rule of law
Identify the problems of the rule of law
Explain the meaning of national development
Explain how democracy and the rule of law promote national development (good governance, employment creation, poverty alleviation, etc.)

topics.name: Political Apathy
objectives: Explain the meaning of political apathy
State the causes of political apathy
State the consequences of political apathy
Explain why leaders fail to protect the interests of their followers
Describe how leaders can protect the interests of their followers
Identify ways of discouraging political apathy

topics.name: Civil Society and Popular Participation
objectives: Explain the meaning of popular participation
Identify the types of popular participation
Explain the need for popular participation in the society
Distinguish traditional and modern modes of popular participation
Describe how popular participation in politics can be achieved
Explain the meaning of civil society
State the functions of and need for civil society
State the qualities/characteristics of civil society, i.e. accountability, fairness, justice, equity, etc.
Identify the problems of civil society, i.e. bribery and corruption, inadequate funding, overbearing influence of foreign donors, etc.

topics.name: Public Service in Democracy
objectives: Explain the meaning of public service
State the functions of public service
Identify the problems of public service
State the reasons for the shortcomings in the public service
Identify ways of improving the public service
